units.Exodus 35:20: Then the whole congregation of the sons of Israel departed from Moses’ presence.

units.Exodus 35:23: Everyone who had fine linen, skins dyed blue, or rams’ skins dyed red brought them.

units.Jeremiah 39:1: The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah in King Zedekiah’s tenth year, which was the eighteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
units.Jeremiah 39:2: The king of Babylon’s force had built siegeworks against Jerusalem, and Jeremiah was kept in the prison court at the king’s house.
units.Jeremiah 39:3: King Zedekiah had shut him in there, saying, Why do you prophesy, saying, Thus said the Lord: I am handing this city over to Babylon’s king, and he will take it?
units.Jeremiah 39:4: Zedekiah will certainly not be saved from the Chaldeans’ hand, but will certainly be handed over to Babylon’s king. His mouth will speak to his mouth, and his eyes will see his eyes.
units.Jeremiah 39:5: Zedekiah will enter Babylon and remain there.
units.Nehemiah 5:1: A great outcry arose from the people and their wives against their Jewish brothers.
units.Nehemiah 5:2: Some said, “With our sons and daughters we are many. We must obtain grain, eat, and live.”
units.Nehemiah 5:3: Others said, “Our fields, our vineyards and our houses—we are pledging them. We must obtain grain and eat.”
units.Nehemiah 5:5: Now our flesh is like our brothers’ flesh, and our sons like their sons. Yet we are forcing our sons and daughters into slavery, and some of our daughters are being subjected. There is no power in our hands, and our fields and vineyards belong to the honored men.”
units.Nehemiah 5:6: I was deeply grieved when I heard their outcry and these words.
units.Nehemiah 5:7: My heart took counsel within me. I contended with the honored men and leaders and said to them, “You are making demands, each against his brother!” I brought a great assembly against them,
units.Nehemiah 5:8: and said to them, “We have bought our Jewish brothers who were being sold to the nations, of our own free will. And are you selling your brothers?” They fell quiet and found no answer.
units.Nehemiah 5:9: I said, “What you are doing is not good. Not so! In the fear of our God you shall depart from the reproach of the nations, our enemies.
units.Nehemiah 5:10: My brothers, my acquaintances and I have also put silver and grain at their disposal. Let us, I pray, relinquish this exaction.
units.Nehemiah 5:11: Please restore to them this very day their fields, vineyards, olive trees and houses; and from the silver, bring out for them the grain, wine and oil.”
units.Nehemiah 5:12: They said, “We will return it and ask nothing from them. We will do as you say.” I called the priests and made them swear to act according to this word.
units.Nehemiah 5:13: I shook out my wrap and said, “So may God shake out from his house and his labor every man who does not uphold this word. So shall he be shaken out and empty.” All the assembly said, “Amen,” and praised the Lord. The people carried out this word.
units.Nehemiah 5:14: From the day he appointed me to be their ruler in the land of Judah—from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of Arthasastha, twelve years—I and my brothers did not eat their coerced provision,
units.Nehemiah 5:15: and as for the former exactions, which before me they laid heavily upon them: they took from them bread and wine, and, at the last, silver—forty didrachms. Their shaken-out men exercise authority over the people, but I did not act that way, because of the fear of God.
units.Nehemiah 5:17: At my table were the Jews, one hundred and fifty men, and those who came to us from the nations around us.
units.Nehemiah 5:18: Each day one young bull, six choice sheep and a he-goat were prepared for me. Every ten days there was wine in abundance for everyone. Along with these things, I did not demand bread from coercion, because the service weighed heavily on this people.
units.Nehemiah 5:19: Remember me for good, God, for everything I have done for this people.
units.2 Kings 23:31: Joachas was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Amital daughter of Jeremiah, from Lemna.
units.2 Kings 23:32: He did what was evil in the Lord’s eyes, according to everything his fathers had done.
units.2 Kings 23:33: Pharaoh Nechao removed him at Deblatha in Emath’s land so that he would not reign in Jerusalem. He imposed a penalty on the land of one hundred talents of silver and one hundred talents of gold.
units.2 Kings 23:34: Pharaoh Nechao made Eliakim, son of Josiah king of Judah, king over them in place of his father Josiah and changed his name to Joakim. He took Joachas and brought him into Egypt, and he died there.
units.2 Kings 23:35: Joakim gave the silver and gold to Pharaoh, but assessed the land to provide the silver at Pharaoh’s command. Each according to his assessment, they gave the silver and gold with the people of the land, to give to Pharaoh Nechao.

units.Exodus 18:13: After the next day Moses sat to judge the people, and all the people stood before Moses from morning until evening.
units.Exodus 18:14: And when Jethro saw all that he did to the people, he said, “What is this that you do to the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand before you from morning until evening?”
units.Exodus 18:15: Moses said to his father-in-law, “The people come to me to seek judgment from God.
units.Exodus 18:16: When they have a dispute and come to me, I judge each case and instruct them in God’s ordinances and His law.”
units.Exodus 18:17: And Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “You are not doing this rightly.
units.Exodus 18:18: You shall be worn out with unbearable exhaustion, both you and all this people who are with you; this matter is heavy for you, and you cannot do it alone.
units.Exodus 18:19: Now therefore listen to me, and I will counsel you, and God shall be with you. Represent the people in matters pertaining to God, and bring their words to God.
units.Exodus 18:20: And you shall solemnly instruct them in the ordinances of God and His law, and show them the ways in which they shall walk, and the works which they shall do.
units.Exodus 18:21: And choose for yourself from all the people able men who fear God, righteous men who hate arrogance; and you shall set them over the people as rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, and rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
units.Exodus 18:22: And they shall judge the people at all times; the weighty matter they shall bring to you, but the lesser judgments they shall judge themselves; and they shall lighten your burden, and bear it with you.
units.Exodus 18:23: If you do this thing, God shall strengthen you, and you shall be able to stand; and all this people shall come to their own place in peace.”
units.Exodus 18:24: Moses listened to his father-in-law and did all that he said.
units.Exodus 18:25: Moses chose capable men from all Israel and appointed them over the people as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
units.Exodus 18:26: They judged the people at all times. They brought every weighty matter to Moses, but judged every light matter themselves.

reread_versions.relationship: Shared named landmark in accounts of the city's rebuilding
reread_versions.rationale: Nehemiah locates priestly repairs above the Horse Gate. Jeremiah's description of a city to be built for the Lord includes the corner of the eastern Horse Gate in its sacred boundary. The named gate provides a particular geographical connection; the repair notice does not establish every boundary, the exact architecture, or the fulfilment of the promise that the city will never be torn down.

reread_versions.relationship: Royal monetary demands borne by the land's people
reread_versions.rationale: The speakers borrow silver for the king's taxes, putting their property at stake. Joakim assesses the land so that its people provide silver and gold demanded by Pharaoh. Both show royal monetary demands falling upon the population and its resources. The rulers, assessments and occasions differ, and Kings does not say those payers borrowed or pledged their property.

reread_versions.relationship: A leader's account of restraint from personal gain
reread_versions.rationale: Within his account of governing Judah, the narrator says that he acquired no field. Samuel publicly asks whether he has taken anyone's animals or payments, and the people deny that he has taken anything from them. Both present restraint from personal gain as part of an account of public service; the field claim is not substituted for Samuel's particular assets, and no change is made to Nehemiah's opening statement about the wall work.

reread_versions.relationship: Fear of God as a qualification for delegated authority
reread_versions.rationale: Anania, the ruler of the bira, is commended as truthful and fearing God more than many when the Jerusalem gate arrangements are entrusted to the officials. Jethro advises Moses to choose rulers who fear God, are righteous and hate arrogance. Both attach fear of God to delegated responsibility, while city security and judicial administration remain distinct and the differently worded additional virtues are preserved.
